deliverables: Open API Layer for Cardano Protocols
12 additional protocol onboardings, three per quarter
MCP server for agents to discover and call published protocols
shared skill framework for all protocols on the registry
documentation, auto-generated SDKs in multiple languages, and live JSON-RPC endpoints
request.recipient: Intersect 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of TxPipe as vendor
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Tx3 by TxPipe: an open, standardized API/interface layer for Cardano dApp protocols with developer and AI-agent access.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,308,000 ADA plus a 327,000 ADA contingency reserve over 12 months, with a total withdrawal of 1,684,050 ADA including a 49,050 ADA Intersect administration fee.
Tx3 is proposed to provide a standard interface that generates documentation, multi-language SDKs, and live JSON-RPC endpoints from verified protocol interface definitions.
The proposer states there is currently no common interface mechanism across Cardano protocols, causing integrators to relearn each protocol and making cross-protocol composability impractical.

The proposal claims AI agents will create increasing on-chain activity and that Cardano protocols need shared deterministic intent and execution interfaces to reduce risks from hallucinated transactions.
TxPipe has already put the developer layer into production with five protocols live on the Tx3 Protocol Registry through Catalyst Fund 14.
The proposal funds 12 additional protocol onboardings, at three per quarter, with full developer and agent coverage plus MCP server and skill-framework development.
The proposer states the action achieved the required 67% support threshold in the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposer states the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at submission.

TxPipe is stated to have received funding through 30 Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and four under development on schedule, plus 2025 Intersect maintenance funding delivered on schedule.

The proposal states that funds will be administered through Intersect treasury smart contracts with milestone-based disbursement controls, an external oversight committee, published permissions, audit references, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document requests 1,684,050 ADA for a 12-month TxPipe Tx3 expansion administered by Intersect, centered on standardized protocol interfaces, SDKs, RPC endpoints, agent-facing documentation, protocol skills, and an MCP server, with claims of prior production deployment, budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and smart-contract-based oversight.
